telegram.helpTitle: How do I get a bot token and chat ID?
telegram.help1: In Telegram, open <c>@BotFather</c>, send <c>/newbot</c> and follow the steps. BotFather replies with the bot token (e.g. <c>123456789:AAE…</c>). Keep it secret.
telegram.help2: Private chat: open your bot and press Start. Group: add the bot to the group and send a message there. Channel: add the bot as an administrator.
telegram.help3: Then open the following address in a browser and copy the number after <c>"id"</c> in the <c>"chat"</c> section:
telegram.help4: Group and channel IDs are negative (supergroups start with <c>-100</c>). For a public channel you can also use <c>@channelname</c>.
telegram.botTokenHint: From <c>@BotFather</c>. Write-only: it is never shown again.
telegram.tokenInvalid: Expected digits, a colon and the key, e.g. 123456789:AAE…
telegram.chatIdHint: <c>-100…</c> for groups/channels, a number for a private chat, or <c>@channelname</c>

escalation.title: Escalation and reminders
escalation.help: Escalation sends the problem to more channels when it is neither acknowledged nor recovered after the given time (measured from when the problem began). Reminders repeat the notification to the rule channels. Both stop when the problem is acknowledged, recovers, or the device is in maintenance.
escalation.afterHint: From the start of the problem; at least the delay above (1 minute to 7 days).
escalation.channelsHint: Who gets the escalation (e.g. the on-call manager). The recovery is sent to them too.
escalation.repeatHint: Sent to the rule channels; 5 minutes to 7 days.

err.afterDelay: Must be at least the delay.

features.title: Features
features.intro: Every feature of this release is off by default. Turning one on or off takes effect immediately, without a restart; stored data is kept while a feature is off. Features with a settings tab of their own are switched in that tab.
features.askAdmin: Ask an administrator to turn it on.

desc.traps: Receive SNMP traps (v1/v2c/v3) from devices, store and search them.
desc.syslog: Receive syslog messages (UDP and TCP), store and search them.
desc.event_alerts: Turn traps and syslog messages into alerts through event rules (event sensors per device).
desc.lag: Show link aggregation (LAG/trunk) membership in the ports view.
desc.ldap: Let Active Directory users sign in with their domain account (local accounts keep working).
desc.audit: Record who changed what, and every login, in a tamper-proof audit log.
desc.timeline: A per-device timeline of status changes, notifications, traps, syslog and changes.
desc.teams: Send notifications to a Microsoft Teams channel (Workflows webhook).
desc.flapping: Detect ports that go up and down repeatedly and hold back their link alerts.
desc.siem_forwarding: Forward received traps and syslog to a SIEM (RFC 5424 over UDP, TCP or TLS).
desc.api_tokens: Personal tokens for scripts and integrations (Authorization: Bearer).

hint.needsIngest: Needs SNMP traps or Syslog to be on to receive anything.
hint.noTargets: No forwarding targets yet: add them under SIEM forwarding.
hint.flappingTraps: Uses linkUp/linkDown traps when SNMP traps are on, plus interface sensors and the port inventory.

hint.timelineSources: Traps, syslog and audit entries appear when those features are on.
hint.lagPorts: Uses the port inventory (devices with ports enabled).

logs.title: Traps & Syslog

rangeErr.invalid: Enter a valid start (and end) time.
rangeErr.order: The end must be after the start.
rangeErr.tooLong: The range may be at most 31 days.

logs.liveHint: Show new records as they arrive
logs.liveNeedsOpenRange: Live needs a range that ends now (a preset or a custom range without end)
logs.empty: No syslog messages in this range.

unknownSources.intro: Senders that are not a monitored device (by host or additional source address). Assign them to a device or ignore them.
unknownSources.assignHint: The address is added to the device's additional source addresses; new records are attributed to it.
unknownSources.ignored: Source added to the ignore list.
unknownSources.viewerHint: Only administrators can assign or ignore sources.

eventRules.builtinNoDelete: Built-in rules can be disabled or reset, not deleted
eventRules.orderHint: Rules are evaluated top to bottom; the first matching rule raises the condition. Drag (or use the arrows) to reorder.
eventRules.editClearsConditions: Saving changes removes this rule's active conditions.
eventRules.textHint: Contained in the message (case-insensitive); empty = any.
eventRules.trapOidsHint: One prefix per line; empty = any trap.
eventRules.portsHint: Important: uplinks, LAGs and ports with an interface sensor.

actionHint.warning: Raises a warning condition on the device's event sensor.
actionHint.down: Raises a down condition on the device's event sensor.
actionHint.ignore: Matching messages stop here; later rules are not evaluated.

eventRules.keyVarbindHint: Tracks instances separately (e.g. ifIndex: port 5 and port 7).
eventRules.keyRegexHint: Exactly one capture group, e.g. interface (\S+)
eventRules.clearingHint: A condition must be able to end: clear on a matching message and/or automatically.
eventRules.clearOnMatch: Clear on a matching message (same key)
eventRules.testHint: Run the rule against the stored records of the last 24 h (no side effects)

err.keyGroup: The key regex needs exactly one capture group.
err.needClear: Warning/down rules need a clear match or an auto-clear time.

conditions.title: Active conditions
conditions.none: No active conditions — the sensor is up.
conditions.introGeneric: The sensor's status is the worst active condition.

intro.trap: Conditions raised by trap rules. The sensor's status is the worst active condition.
intro.syslog: Conditions raised by syslog rules. The sensor's status is the worst active condition.
intro.port_flap: Ports that are flapping. Link alerts of these ports are held back until they are stable again.

flapping.title: Port flapping
flapping.intro: A port is flapping after {{n}} up/down changes within {{w}} min; it is stable again after {{q}} min without a change.

ingest.title: Ingest status
ingest.nat: Several devices seem to send from one address ({{addr}}) — probably NAT. Records from it cannot be attributed reliably.
ingest.noTrgm: Text search is slower: the pg_trgm extension is not available.

ingestSettings.title: Traps & syslog

unknownHint.store: Stored without a device; assign them later.
unknownHint.drop: Records from unknown senders are dropped (counted).

checkHint.any: v1/v2c traps are accepted with any community.
checkHint.known: v1/v2c traps with another community are dropped.

ingestSettings.knownNeedsList: Add at least one community first.

v3.title: SNMPv3 trap users
v3.hint: Keys are write-only: leave empty to keep the stored key.

linkScope.title: Link alerts
linkScope.label: Link-down and flapping alerts cover
linkScope.importantHint: Uplinks, LAGs and ports with an interface sensor — no alert for every PC switched off at night.
linkScope.allHint: Every port that goes down or flaps raises an alert.

siem.title: SIEM forwarding
siem.intro: Accepted traps and syslog records are forwarded as RFC 5424 syslog, preserving the original sender (up to 4 targets).
siem.minSeverityHint: Forward records of this severity and worse.
siem.tlsVerifyOff: The certificate is not verified: the connection can be intercepted.
siem.udpHint: UDP gives no delivery guarantee; prefer TCP or TLS.

ldap.title: Active Directory
ldap.intro: AD users sign in with DOMAIN\user or user@domain. Local accounts always keep working, and a local administrator must always exist. Test before you turn the feature on.
ldap.serversHint: host or host:port, one per line (≤ 8); empty = find by DNS. Use the names in the DC certificates.
ldap.tlsVerifyOff: Certificates are not verified: passwords could be intercepted.
ldap.passwordUnreadable: The stored service account password cannot be decrypted (the server key changed). Enter it again — AD logins fail until then.
ldap.groupsHint: Members (also nested) of the admin group become administrators, of the viewer group viewers.
ldap.testHint: Tests use the values in the form (not yet saved); they work while the feature is off.
ldap.testUserHint: Checks a user's sign-in step by step. No user is created; the password is not stored or logged.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.retentionHint: 30–3650; old entries are deleted by the retention job only.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.intro: Personal tokens for scripts: send them as Authorization: Bearer. A token never has more rights than you.
tokens.nameHint: What the token is for, e.g. backup-script.
tokens.showOnce: Copy the token now — it is shown only this once.
tokens.revokeConfirm: Revoke "{{name}}"? Scripts using it stop working at once.
